input.question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?
input.ground_truth: Because you remember the best, eventful memories in more detail. You tend to block out all the normal things like changing you socks or taking a shit that day. Similar to when you zone out in the shower trying to think if you've just washed your hair or not. You do those things everyday and block them out of memory.

Question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy box. When you play with your toys every day, sometimes they get a little dirty or broken, and you might not think they are so special anymore. But if you put the toys away for a long time and then look at them later, you only remember how cool and fun they were when you first got them. You forget about the times they were a little boring or broken.

So, when we remember things from the past, like a fun day at the park or a birthday party, we mostly remember the happy and good parts. We don’t remember as much the times we were bored or sad. That’s why things from the past seem a lot better than they really were!
